object_description: quiet compact three-storey volume with a set-back ground floor and an aluminium curtain skin
geometry_property: set-back ground floor on the long side
recessed on the other side for a covered area
aluminium panel skin with garland-like ends
design_condition: the quiet three-storey volume completes the group around the existing tower at regular distances from its neighbours, setting back its ground floor to reveal the entrances and shelter the garage doors on the other side

positive: A quiet three-storey volume with regular distances from the neighbours completes the existing group
The slightly set-back ground floor makes the two entrances visible
The vehicle hall stretches from facade to facade between the two stairwell cores
A clear concept is visible in both the static structure and the distribution of use
An upper band of windows keeps the facade from appearing forbidding
It additionally illuminates the hall without allowing unwanted views
On the other long side the volume recedes in favour of a covered area in front of the garage doors
This overhang adds additional value to the work area
The simple access structure allows flexible use of floor units
An atrium and a skylight bring daylight into the unexposed central zone
The steel trusses in the attic with suspended floor ceilings are carefully constructed
The structure is architecturally crucial for the spatial expression
The construction is very simple and pragmatically implemented
The compact structure is fundamentally aimed at good economic efficiency
The favourable facade construction and short construction period give medium economic efficiency
The project stands out due to its simple setting, efficient static solution and clear distribution of use
negative: The uneven volume shifts resulting from use make one street view appear unsettled
No statements are made about the design of the surroundings
The curtain facade theme is interpreted almost literally with garland-like ends
The round windows may be an eye-catcher but give the reading room too little connection to the outside
The facade expression is independent but has little to do with the location and surrounding buildings
A change of use would require windows in front of the trusses, severely disrupting the facade
The generous simplicity of the structure creates possibilities not necessary for the intended uses
A lack of energy concept shows in undersized technology centres and hard-to-access basement shafts
The lightweight shell for the archive increases technical effort and energy needs for the archive climate
The economic advantage is offset by the large spans of the supporting structure
The promising approach is not reflected in the architectural design
